title: Sopris Capital buys Blackford Analysis from Bayer
source_used: Sopris Capital press release (PR Newswire) as carried by Yahoo Finance UK; AuntMinnie, PE Hub, citybiz blocked or paywalled
key_facts: Sopris Capital, a multi-strategy investment firm with healthcare technology holdings, announced on 9 Oct 2026 that it completed the acquisition of Blackford Analysis from Bayer.
Blackford, founded in 2010, runs an AI orchestration platform for medical imaging, used by equipment makers and hospitals.
The Blackford platform holds more than 130 AI applications from over 45 partner vendors, giving health systems a single vendor-neutral way to bring AI into radiology work.
Sopris is combining Blackford under its portfolio company Azra AI, expected within days or weeks; Blackford stays a separate legal entity with operations in Scotland and the US.
The release says there will be no disruption to current deployments; terms of the deal are not given.
quote_evidence: Sopris Capital ... today announced it has completed the acquisition of Blackford Analysis from Bayer.
Blackford will continue to operate as a separate legal entity following the combination with operations in Scotland and the United States.
The Blackford Platform has a portfolio of more than 130 AI applications from over 45 partner vendors.
why_it_matters_hint: Software that lets hospitals run many imaging AI tools changes owner as Bayer exits.
notes: Press release is paid content; text read via Yahoo Finance UK (a copy site), original is Sopris Capital's PR Newswire release. AuntMinnie and PE Hub headlines confirm the deal; their text was blocked or behind a login.
